text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000181 bills 99215 well above its risk-adjusted expectation in every complexity band, but only five documented 99215 charts exist (all supporting the billed level), so upcoding cannot be confirmed or ruled out.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"Most of this provider's 99215s fall on patients with five or more conditions, and the low-complexity share is small, which fits a genuinely sick panel. However, the risk-adjusted excess persists within every complexity band, roughly double the all-provider share even among patients with 0–2 conditions, so panel acuity alone does not explain the pattern. The records review cuts the other way: no documented claim at any level fell below the billed level, and the 99215 examples show high MDM with 42–54 minutes. But five documented 99215s is far too thin to judge, and the two notes claiming moderate-or-higher data review with no lab or test line on the claim are only weak evidence of note inflation. A reviewer should first request charts for the sampled low-complexity 99215s, such as C0104645 and C0105873 (back pain, no chronic conditions), C0104701 (abdominal pain) and C0104770 (UTI in an 18-year-old), and should expand the record sample until the documented 99215 rate can be meaningfully compared to the peer rate."}
